questions.enonce_markdown: Ethanol is manufactured from starch by fermentation. With the help of chemical equations, describe the manufacturing process. *[18 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Starch (from maize, cassava, potatoes or rice) is converted to ethanol in four stages.

**1. Preparation.** The starch is crushed, mixed with water and heated (cooked) to burst the grains and form a suspension.

**2. Hydrolysis of starch to maltose** by the enzyme **diastase (amylase)**, from germinating barley (malt), at about $50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$:

$\mathrm{2(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n + nH_2O \rightarrow nC_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$

**3. Hydrolysis of maltose to glucose** by the enzyme **maltase** (present in yeast):

$\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \rightarrow 2C_6H_{12}O_6}$

**4. Fermentation of glucose to ethanol** by the enzyme **zymase** in yeast, at $25 - 35^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, in the **absence of air**, for several days:

$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2}$

(Checks: starch to maltose: C $12n$, H $20n + 2n = 22n$, O $10n + n = 11n$; maltose to glucose: C 12, H 24, O 12 on both sides; fermentation: C 6, H 12, O 6 on both sides.)

The temperature is kept moderate because the enzymes are destroyed above about $40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, and fermentation stops when the ethanol concentration reaches about 15 % (the alcohol kills the yeast).

**5. Separation.** The dilute ethanol solution (the "wash") is purified by **fractional distillation**: ethanol (boiling point $78^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) distils off before water (boiling point $100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) to give a mixture of about 95 % ethanol.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two large scale uses of ethanol obtained in this way. *[2 marks]*
